title: kubelet coldstart init lab transcript
content:
Context:
- Running a small lab repro of a customer-facing node provisioning failure. Behavior: newly provisioned nodes boot, cloud-init runs, join control plane via kubeadm/cluster-provisioner, but never reach Ready. Symptoms are a mix of kubelet cold-start crashes and missing block device mounts for ephemeral root volumes.

Timeline / commands + outputs (raw-ish):
2024-11-02 09:12 AM - first boot (VM powered up)
$ sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b | sed -n '1,120p'
-- Logs begin at Fri 2024-11-01 23:51:09 UTC, end at Sat 2024-11-02 09:20:11 UTC. --
Nov 02 09:13:02 node-07 kubelet[2345]: E1102 09:13:02.123456 2345 server.go:500] failed to run Kubelet: failed to create pod infra container: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create containerd task: OCI runtime create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: mount failed: /var/lib/kubelet/pods/...: device or resource busy
Nov 02 09:13:02 node-07 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=255/n/a
Nov 02 09:13:02 node-07 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.

$ sudo systemctl status kubelet
● kubelet.service - kubelet: Kubernetes Node Agent
   Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
   Active: failed (Result: exit-code) since Sat 2024-11-02 09:13:02 UTC; 1min 30s ago

$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep node-07 || true
(node not listed)  # node didn't successfully register with API server

Check container runtime:
$ sudo crictl ps -a
FATA[0000] failed to connect to runtime: context deadline exceeded
-> suspected containerd didn't come up or socket path mismatch

Reading cloud-init logs: /var/log/cloud-init-output.log
cloud-init: INFO: executing userdata...
cloud-init: ERROR: failed to mount /dev/sdb on /mnt/ephemeral: mount: special device /dev/sdb does not exist

lsblk output (node-07):
NAME   MAJ:MIN RM  SIZE RO TYPE MOUNTPOINT
sda      8:0    0   50G  0 disk 
sda1     8:1    0  200M  0 part /boot/efi
sda2     8:2    0 49.8G  0 part /
(there's no sdb)

Hypothesis at this point: provisioning expects ephemeral disk attached as /dev/sdb but underlying cloud provider didn't attach it (or device name changed e.g. /dev/nvme1n1). cloud-init tries to mount wrong device and leaves node in weird state; kubelet then starts but can't create pod infra because /var/lib/kubelet is on ephemeral device expected to be present.

Commands I tried to iterate: (notes and rationale)
1) probe for available block devices (nvme detection)
$ sudo ls /dev/nvme* || true
# output: /dev/nvme0n1 exists with partitions nvme0n1p1 nvme0n1p2 -> ephemeral ended up as nvme device 

2) quick workaround (manual): create symlink so cloud-init mount path resolves
$ sudo ln -s /dev/nvme0n1 /dev/sdb && sudo mount /dev/sdb /mnt/ephemeral
- After mounting, re-run kubelet start: sudo systemctl restart kubelet
- kubelet progressed further but later failed with: Nov 02 09:22:13 kubelet[2456]: E1102 09:22:13.987654 2456 kubelet.go:248] container runtime is down: runtime status check failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded

3) check containerd logs
$ sudo journalctl -u containerd -b | tail -n 80
Nov 02 09:21:58 node-07 containerd[1987]: time="2024-11-02T09:21:58Z" level=error msg="failed to create shim task: runc create failed: exit status 1: runc: unable to mkdir: permission denied"
-> appears to be permission errors in /run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task which looked like wrong SELinux or tmpfs mount flags in our custom image.

4) inspect kubelet flags (systemd service file override created by provisioning)
$ cat /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-provision.conf
Environment=KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--cgroup-driver=systemd --root-dir=/var/lib/kubelet
# root-dir is default, but provisioning sometimes sets it to an ephemeral mount path (bad)

5) check /var/lib/kubelet
$ df -h /var/lib/kubelet || true
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/nvme0n1p2  47G   12G   34G  26% /
-> /var/lib/kubelet is on root, not ephemeral. But earlier cloud-init logs showed attempts to format ephemeral and move kubelet root there. Looks like partial provisioning state machine: moved files, restarted kubelet during the move and left things half-done.

Reproduce steps in lab (what I ran):
- fresh VM image built from packer: image-v2024-10-30 with cloud-init user-data from infra repo (GH: redwood/infra/blob/main/packer/userdata/node-init.yaml)
- attach ephemeral disk (AWS instance-store or c5d ephemeral) via terraform profile ephemeral-attach=true
- boot VM, wait for cloud-init to partition and format /dev/sdb and mount to /mnt/ephemeral, then rsync /var/lib/kubelet to ephemeral and create systemd override to set root-dir=/mnt/ephemeral/kubelet

Observed flakiness: sometimes /dev/sdb appears as /dev/nvme1n1 after kernel enumerates -> cloud-init script looks up by name (/dev/sdb) not by UUID or nvme serial -> race condition. If cloud-init runs early before nvme driver finished, device not present, script logs and continues (doesn't retry), leaving mapping inconsistent.

Errors seen in API server once node attempted to register:
- TLS cert rotation errors (kubelet couldn't read certs in new location)
- kube-proxy failing to start because CNI config missing (cloud-init also copies CNI to ephemeral path but didn't finish)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) root cause: cloud-init device detection logic is fragile (assumes /dev/sdb). When kernel assigns nvme devices, name differs; provisioning script doesn't retry/wait -> half-baked migration of kubelet root-dir -> kubelet crashes. (HIGH)
2) secondary contributor: container runtime permissions mis-set in image (tmpfs or SELinux labels) causing containerd to fail creating runtime dirs, amplifying the initial failure. (MEDIUM)
3) rarer bug: kubeadm join timing + TLS provisioning bug if kubelet restarts during cert write -> cert files left with wrong permissions. (LOW)

Temporary mitigations I tested: (ordered by invasiveness)
- Option A (quick): modify cloud-init to detect NVMe by serial or wait loop: 'for i in {1..10}; do ls /dev/nvme* && break || sleep 3; done' -> reduces incidence in lab.
- Option B: change provisioning to mount ephemeral under /mnt/ephemeral but keep kubelet root on / -> avoid moving kubelet data during first-boot; instead have migration job that runs after node is Ready.
- Option C: image hardening: ensure containerd dirs exist and are chowned to containerd user before first start. Also set SELinux permissive in image if we can't reproduce the policy correctly.

Commands to gather more signal (TODOs):
- Add a boot-time script to dump /proc/partitions and /dev/disk/by-id/* to /var/log/provision-devices.log
- Collect cloud-init logs and archive when provisioning fails: /var/log/cloud-init.log, cloud-init-output.log, /var/log/installer.log
- Capture kernel ring buffer at first boot: dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg-boot.txt (for NVMe driver initialization timing)
- For a controlled repro, create a small loopback block device and ensure cloud-init uses by-uuid mount detection rather than static /dev name.

Concrete next steps for infra follow-up:
- [Diego] update cloud-init script to detect block devices by LABEL/UUID and add a retry loop (PR: GH: redwood/infra#2147)
- [Sanjay] build a small baked image with containerd permissions pre-fixed and boot a 10-node batch to validate (image: image-v2024-11-20-test)
- [Ava] add additional logging to provisioning pipeline to capture /dev listings and containerd journal at the time of failure, post to INC-4821 for incident correlation.

One-liner root cause hypothesis to communicate to product/CS: provisioning script assumes stable device name for ephemeral storage and migrates kubelet files prematurely; when kernel assigns a different device name (common for NVMe), the migration partially fails and kubelet enters a crash loop that prevents node registration.

Notes / random debugging artifacts:
- I saw one case where cloud-init created /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-provision.conf with root-dir=/mnt/ephemeral/kubelet but left that mountpoint empty -> kubelet started and then container runtime created files under root /var/lib/containerd while kubelet expected them on ephemeral -> double-write weirdness.
- Docker vs containerd: our fleet is containerd; don't test with docker. crictl is the right tool.
- CNI: validate that /etc/cni/net.d/10-calico.conflist is copied before kubelet starts; if not, kubelet registers but pods stay Pending which looks like a different failure mode.

Quick checklist for remediation PR: (to include in GH PR description)
- replace /dev/sdb references with discovery by ID or wait loop
- ensure cloud-init aborts on partial failure or performs atomic swap (move into tmp dir then move into final path)
- add prestart hook for containerd in systemd unit that ensures required dirs exist and are properly chowned
- add validation step to provisioning that waits for node to reach Ready before marking provisioned in our control plane

Closing thought: this one is messy because multiple race conditions and permission assumptions interact. Fix the device detection first (high ROI) and then address containerd perms. Keep this doc as the lab transcript so we can paste examples back into the PR and the incident ticket.

Unresolved questions:
- Why sometimes /dev/sdb is present and sometimes not? (cloud-provider agent vs kernel nvme init ordering). Need to test with slower boot and simulated NVMe latency.
- Are there AWS instance types where ephemeral appears consistently as /dev/sdb? (old paravirtual naming)

Saved commands to reproduce quickly (for my notes):
- packer build -var 'image_tag=test-ephemeral' ./images/node-image.json
- terraform apply -var 'ephemeral_attach=true' -var 'instance_type=c5d.large' ./tf/ephemeral-test
- ssh into vm and tail cloud-init: sudo tail -f /var/log/cloud-init-output.log

End of transcript - will add links to PR and incident when created.
